text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Coalition pressures could delay round of cabinet appointments.
- Cabinet minister Rafael Eitan proposes Ateret Cohanim settler group build hot houses in Abu Dis.
- Treasury officials estimate Netanyahu will back off from making additional budget cut.
- Health Ministry ignored hundreds of malpractice suits this year.
JERUSALEM POST
- Coalition legislators to vote no-confidence.
- Cabinet reshuffle likely to be delayed.
- Pupils' math, science add up to mediocrity.
- Court bars crocodile wrestling.
- Treasury: At least two billion shekel cut in 1998 budget.
- Tadiran opens Moscow office.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Pressure on Netanyahu ahead of cabinet appointments.
- Israeli Ambassador to U.S. in message to Israel: "I told Albright that we are not building in the territories; In truth, I don't know if we are building."
- Secret Pentagon conference turned Royal Beach hotel in Eilat into fortress.
MAARIV
- Arafat: "We arrested a woman suicide bomber on her way to Israel."
- Israeli Health Ministry to demand billions from cigarette manufacturers after U.S. agreement.
